J U D G M E N T/Awar D
1.

Vide this judgment/award, I shall dispose off Mact Claim Petition filed under Section 163-A
Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as M.V. Act), in regard to death of Sh. Hari Lal
, (in short, the deceased),
who allegedly died in a road vehicular accident on 21.07.2023.
2. Brief facts as per claim petition are that on 20.07.2013 deceased boarded a bus bearing no. UP 42T 7279 from Ashok Vihar Bus Stand Delhi to his native village Sultanpur to see his ailing mother.
On 21.07.2013, the body of deceased was found lying at Haidergarh Bus Stand.
FIR no. 145/2013 was registered at PS Haidargarh, Barabank, UP for the offences punishable under Section 118/176 IPC.
PM on the body of deceased was conducted vide report no. 478/2013 as per which the cause of death was due to coma as a result of antimortem head injuries.

MACT Case No. 585/18 (FIR no. 145/2013) Kusum Lata vs. Kendriya Prabhair (Sultanpur Depot)

UP 42T 7279 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle) as driver/R3 was driving the offending vehicle in zig zag manner and also applied sudden brakes due to which head of deceased hit against the floor of the bus and he succumbed to the injuries.
4. As per claim petition deceased is survived by his wife and three children.
5. WS was filed on behalf of R1 claiming that that no accident was caused with offending vehicle.
R2 & R3 have also adopt the WS filed on behalf of R3.

EVIDENCE:
7.
In evidence, petitioners have examined themselves as Pw1 to Pw4 respectively.
They are not the eye witness of the accident.

They have proved the documents Ex.Pw1/1 to Ex.Pw1/8 which are also exhibited as Pw3/1 to Ex.Pw3/8 & Ex.Pw4/1 to Ex.Pw4/7.
8.
Petitioners have also examined Sh. Satyam Tiwari as Pw5 who filed his affidavit Ex.Pw5/A and he proved his complaint Ex.Pw5/2.

He deposed that on 21.07.2013 at about 03:00 -03:30 am, he was present at the spot to drop the relative of his friend and saw that driver/R1 and conductor of offending vehicle were putting out the body of deceased from the offending vehicle by holding his hands and legs.
Seeing the public persons at the spot, driver and conductor fled away from the spot.
9. In respondents evidence, R3 has examined himself as R1w1 and filed his affidavit Ex.Rw1/A.
He admitted that he was driver of the offending vehicle on 21.07.2013
He denied that deceased was travelling in the offending vehicle or that he alongwith conductor of the offending vehicle left the deceased on the road unattended.
He admitted that police officials of PS Haidergarh enquired him with respect to the alleged incident.
He denied that UPSRTC deliberately not conducted any inquiry.

10. R3 has also examined Sh. Ashish Kumar Srivastava as R1w2 who MACT Case No. 585/18 (FIR no. 145/2013) Kusum Lata vs. Kendriya Prabhair (Sultanpur Depot) Page no. 4 of 7 VIKRAM 2026.02.05 was conductor on the offending vehicle.

12. I have heard Ld. Counsel for the parties and have gone through the testimony of witnesses including the pleadings and the documents.

My issue wise findings in the case are as under:-

13.

It is well settled that the procedure followed for proceedings conducted by an accident tribunal is similar to that followed by a civil court and in civil matters the facts are required to be established by preponderance of probabilities only and not by strict rules of evidence or beyond reasonable doubts as are required in a criminal prosecution.

The burden of proof in a civil case is never as heavy as that is required in a criminal case, but in a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, this burden is infact even lesser than that in a civil case.

Himachal Road Transport Corporation and others, reported in (2009) 13 SC 530, which were reiterated in the subsequent judgment in the case of Parmeshwari Vs. Amir Chand and others 2011 (1) SCR 1096 (Civil Appeal No.1082 of 2011) and also in another case Mangla Ram Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd.
& Ors., 2018 Law Suit (SC) 303.

sentences.text: Petitioners have examined Pw-5 Satyam Tiwari to prove the case who deposed that on the day of incident he was present at the spot and saw that R3/driver and conductor of the offending vehicle taking the dead body of deceased off the offending vehicle and on seeing the public persons, they fled away from the spot.
He himself admitted that his statement was not recorded by police nor he is witness in criminal case.
Pw-5 also proved a complaint Ex.Pw5/2 addressed to SHO, Kotawali Haidargarh, UP with respect to the present accident.
However, the same was made on 11.04.2023 after around 10 years of the incident.

The said witness appears to be an interested witness as he himself deposed in his testimony that he met with the son of deceased on 05.01.2023 at Sultanpur and thereafter he made complaint Ex.Pw5/2 to SHO, Kotwali Haidergarh on 11.04.2023.
Complaint Ex.Pw5/2 is thus not a reliable document.
No witness is brought on record to prove that the death of deceased was caused due to rash and negligence driving of R3.

Furthermore, petitioner has filed copy of charge sheet on record, as per which she (Kusum Lata) accepted the final report filed by police for want of evidence, stating MACT Case No. 585/18 (FIR no. 145/2013) Kusum Lata vs.
Kendriya Prabhair (Sultanpur Depot) Page no. 6 of 7 VIKRAM 2026.02.05 that she is satisfied with the report filed by police and does not want to contest the case.

Accordingly issue no.1 is decided in favour of the respondents and against the petitioners..
